title: Calculating Compilers
byline: Erik Meijer · PhD thesis, University of Nijmegen, 1992
note: A scanned thesis with an imperfect text layer, so some symbols in the PDF are garbled. Printed page = PDF page − 17; the bibliography (PDF p. 138) and Dutch summary (p. 146) are not broken down. Summaries are in our own words.
summary: Meijer’s thesis argues that compilers should be derived, not just verified: start from a denotational semantics of the source language and transform it by equational reasoning, in the Bird–Meertens style, until it becomes code for an abstract machine, so the result is correct by construction. Chapter 1 does this for a small functional language, ending in de Bruijn-indexed stack code. Chapter 2 is the theory, the famous “bananas, lenses, envelopes and barbed wire” paper: catamorphisms, anamorphisms, hylomorphisms and paramorphisms over algebraic data types in CPO, with their laws. The remaining chapters apply the method to Petri-net update schemes, an imperative language with procedures (via continuations, short-circuit evaluation and tail calls), and backtracking with success and failure continuations and cut.
